newsitem.title: UK: Weak dollar steadies but Euro-stocks slide.
newsitem.headline: Weak dollar steadies but Euro-stocks slide.

text.p: European stocks and bonds fell sharply on Thursday after the dollar came under strong pressure on worries about a possible rise in Japanese interest rates.

Although Germany's central bank kept official interest rates unchanged at its regular council meeting, as expected, the dollar's fall and worldwide interest rate jitters continued to rattle stock and bond markets.
"Bonds and the dollar have led us down across the board," said one London trader about London's blue-chip FTSE-100 index.

Although the dollar later steadied, it remained vulnerable after a senior Japanese official said the currency's recovery from last year's post-war low against the yen was nearly complete and Japan's economy was stronger than markets believed.

"The initial signal did not come from the new U.S. administration as many expected but from Japan, where it appears the groundwork is being laid for a rate hike," said Klaus Baader, senior currency economist at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
By 1230GMT the dollar was quoted at 1.5076 marks and 111.86 yen, compared with 1.5165 marks and 113.83 yen in late European trade on Wednesday.
London markets were also still shaken by Wednesday's Bank of England forecast of an imminent rise in inflation and the probable need for higher interest rates.
Government bond prices worldwide started to reflect these hints of rising interest rates from Japan and Britain and started heading lower, dragging stocks down with them.
The blue-chip FTSE-100 index was down more than three-quarters of a percent, hovering just above session lows by midday.
Some traders also noted pressure on the FTSE coming from derivatives-related selling, including an options trade worth $1.6 billion that is betting on the market falling sharply by next June.

But dealers said the the drop in stocks could be limited because investors were more likely to stay on the sidelines before the rate-setting meeting of the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee on November 13 and Britain's budget on November 26.

Traders said they were looking for U.S. weekly jobless claims and third-quarter productivity and labour costs data due during the afternoon for signs of what might happen on Wall Street following the Dow's 97 point jump on Wednesday.
Germany's DAX index was down more than 0.85 percent, weighed down by a sharp drop in Siemens AG after it forecast output to stay flat in 1996-7.
Paris's blue-chip CAC-40 index was slightly above its lows for the day by mid-session although it was registering a loss of about 0.7 percent.
CURRENCIES AT 1230 GMT
The dollar was at 1.5076 marks and 111.86 yen, compared with 1.5165 marks and 113.83 yen in late European trade on Wednesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1230 GMT
LONDON - The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares was 29.8 points lower at 3,905.9.
PARIS - The CAC-40 share index was down 16.44 at 2,196.93
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index fell 20.64 at 2,708.55.
PRECIOUS METALS
Morning gold fixed at $377.90 against $378.00 previously after it eased overnight on selling in Tokyo and Australian producer sales. Silver was down three cents at $4.75.
